subject: evs
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Know and share personal details: own name, parents' and siblings' names, address, birthday and phone number
Name the main body parts and say what the sense organs and large body parts do
Draw the large parts of the body
Share hobbies, likes and dislikes, and enjoy hearing about other children's
Notice differences among classmates, such as hair, eyes, height and weight
Solve a 6-8 piece body puzzle alone
Name their own feelings and other people's, and begin to manage strong emotions
Take part in small and large group activities and help with shared work
Name family members and say how each one is related to them
Tell a joint family from a nuclear family, and give reasons why families differ
Draw a family tree of grandparents, parents and children
Describe what each family member does and how they help at home
Share the festivals the family celebrates and what they do on them
Name neighbours and friends, and see how neighbours help each other
Play indoor and outdoor games with others, and know the rules
Respect differences in families and treat pets kindly
Name food eaten at home, both raw and cooked, and food made for festivals
Sort foods into those that come from plants and those that come from animals
Give reasons why the food of babies, children and elders is different
Understand why food should not be wasted, and show respect for it
Recognise simple healthy eating habits
Appreciate that families eat different foods
Make rhymes, songs or riddles about food
Name the water sources at home and around them
Describe the different uses of water in the family
Tell apart activities that need water from those that do not
Describe simple things seen about water: colour, taste, smell and shape
Name the containers used to store water and say why water is stored
Suggest ways to re-use water and to avoid wasting it
Describe their own house and name its rooms and the work done in each
Tell apart the different kinds of houses seen around them
Explain why people need a house and why it should be kept clean
Know the use of a dustbin
Name ways to decorate a house, such as with rangoli
Make simple house models and decorations with clay or other materials
Share poems or songs about houses
Explain why people need clothes
Name the clothes worn by themselves, their family and at school
Say which clothes are worn in different seasons, festivals and occasions
Name clothes worn by boys and girls at home
Draw and colour the clothes they wear
Make simple dresses by folding paper (origami)
Know how to keep clothes clean and cared for
Know that air is all around, for example by feeling wind or flying a kite
Name ways living things use air
Give reasons why air becomes dirty
List the harmful effects of unclean air on living things
Try simple activities with air, with help from elders
Understand that planting trees keeps the air clean and fresh

topics.topic: Keeping Oneself Clean, Safe and Healthy
covers: Keep their hands, body, nails, teeth, hair and clothes clean
Keep the house and school surroundings clean and use the dustbin
Name ways to stay healthy: rest, exercise, yoga, deep breathing and play
Play indoor and outdoor games for fun and recreation
Know how to stay safe at home and in public places
Recognise good touch and bad touch, and know to talk to family about them
Do simple exercises and asanas to keep the body fit
Name places nearby, such as school, hospital, park, water bodies, market, bank, post office and bus or railway station
Say what each place is used for in daily life
Name people who work in these places and what they do, such as doctor, teacher, driver and gardener
Say how people in the community keep public places clean
Know how to behave in public places
Show respect for all kinds of work
Know that plants have main parts, and name the plants and trees in school and at home
Tell plants that grow on land from those that grow in water
Name some medicinal plants used in daily life
Name the fruits and vegetables we eat, and the parts of plants we eat as food
Draw and label the main parts of a plant
Care for and protect plants
Name animals and birds seen in their surroundings
Name the main body parts of animals
Tell pet, domestic and wild animals apart, with examples
Name animals and birds that live on land, in water and in the air
Recognise the sounds of common animals and birds, and copy them
Draw and make masks of pet and wild animals
Show care and compassion for animals and birds
Name the modes of transport seen around them, on land, in water and in the air
Name some jobs connected with transport
Give examples of transport used on land, in water and in the air
Say what causes noise around them from vehicles
Know the work of traffic police, traffic lights and emergency vehicles
Suggest ways to reduce smoke and noise from vehicles
Draw and collect pictures of different vehicles
Name ways of communicating at home and in the neighbourhood, such as radio, TV and newspapers
Say what each way of communicating is used for
Understand that messages can be misused
Know, at a simple level, that email, SMS and the internet are ways to communicate
Make poems, songs and drawings about communication

topics.topic: The World Around Me (Sun, Moon, Sky and Stars)
covers: Notice what the sky looks like in the morning, afternoon and at night
Name the sun, moon and stars, and say what each is like
Draw and colour the sun, moon and stars
Describe sunny, cloudy, rainy, summer and winter days in their own words
Share stories, songs and poems about the sky
Make sun, moon and star masks, puppets or collages

gaps: 'Time, Space and Direction' is a theme in the Class II section only, so it is left out of Class I.
